## Execution audit

**Provenance.** All paths below are relative to `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/Documents/Codex/2026-11-02/scene-rsi-rsi-1-3d-blender/`. Expanded files under `outputs/scene_rsi_pilot/results/` correspond to archive members under `experiments/scene_rsi_pilot/results/` with the same remaining path. The r2 sources are in `work/scene_archive/bundles/r2--sceneevolve_cli.tar.gz`; replay sources are in `work/scene_archive/bundles/replay_s1--H_start.tar.gz`. Citations give source ID, path relative to the results directory, and exact lines.

### Window-side kitchen — commons_133800864

The generated scene uses boxes for walls, cabinet doors and 32 tilted blind slats; rods, balls and swept tubes represent the roll, ring, tap and containers. The counter has a Boolean sink cutout; the towel is a collection of separate narrow panels, not simulated cloth. The pitcher and jug are assemblies with specified opacity values (X1237, `r2/sceneevolve_cli/C2/selection/commons_133800864/steps/001/build.py`, lines 22–43, 61–108, 111–145).

Step 2 raised the cabinet bottom to 1.465 and widened the lens from 57 to 49; step 3 shortened the roll, reoriented the ring and towel, moved the jug by (-.16,.04,0), and reduced exposure to -1.15. Its comments report remaining projected discrepancies and a pale appearance; those are author observations, not independent measurements (X1239, same scene `steps/002/build.py`, lines 44–53, 198–204; X1241, `steps/003/build.py`, lines 1–3, 60–95, 137–151, 186–200).

Granite-matching materials receive noise at scale 185 and a color ramp; chrome-matching materials receive metallic .8 and roughness .25. Although step 1 mentions paper grain, the shown node operations implement stone and chrome only. The camera is at (-1.10,-2.25,1.80), with two area lights and a Standard view transform (X1237, `steps/001/build.py`, lines 156–196). The task specifies a 384×512 reference, not necessarily measured output dimensions (X1243, same scene `task.json`, lines 2–5).

All three result files report `ok: true`, null error, empty stderr, 16/16 samples, and saved PNG and blend files; no technical render failure is recorded (X1238, X1240, X1242, respectively `steps/001/result.json`, `steps/002/result.json`, `steps/003/result.json`, lines 2–7). No selection or acceptance record for this scene is supplied.

### Industrial kitchen — commons_138420790

The selected step-3 code builds a box-based island with drawers, timber posts, ceiling beams, dark cabinetry, ovens and a suspended hood. The nominal sink is layered thin boxes and a swept tap, rather than a Boolean-cut basin (X1252, `r2/sceneevolve_cli/C2/selection/commons_138420790/steps/003/build.py`, lines 22–100, 102–145). Step 2 moved the obstructing left wall to x=-8; step 3 kept that placement, changed the lens from 40 to 52 and aim, moved the foreground post, and darkened cabinet and ceiling colors. Its comments claim the wall correction worked and describe remaining reference/render differences; the images are not supplied for independent visual assessment (X1250, `steps/002/build.py`, lines 10–20, 29–32; X1252, `steps/003/build.py`, lines 4–16).

Materials use generated-coordinate noise, color ramp and bump for wood, and fine noise bump for the hood. The scene uses three area lights, AgX and exposure .15 (X1252, `steps/003/build.py`, lines 147–204). All three step results report successful 16-sample renders, saved images and blends, null errors and empty stderr (X1249, X1251, X1253, same scene `steps/001/result.json` through `steps/003/result.json`, lines 2–7). The separate selection file records step 3, although the aggregate record’s `selected` field is null (X1246, `selected.json`, lines 1–3; X1245, `record.json`, lines 53–57).

The record reports overall .4702, SSIM .3208 and LPIPS .7368, plus functional passes for architecture. It explicitly limits those passes to structural/edit operability; semantic completeness and support/collision truth are null. Render history identifies CUDA A100, while functional checking fell back to CPU because the authorized GPU became busy—not a recorded rendering failure (X1245, `record.json`, lines 16–34, 58–68, 156–170).

### Archive corridor — commons_2238909

The replay’s selected step is 3 (X1257, `replay_s1/H_start/H_start/replay_development/commons_2238909/selected.json`, lines 1–3). Its top-level build specifies 25 repeated shelving-bank assemblies, with separate wheels, hubs, arms, grips and plaques; a book bay, carts and fluorescent fixtures are also assembled from primitives (X1255, same scene `build.py`, lines 38–98, 100–152). It sets emissive bright materials, a 30 mm camera, area lights, and Cycles 512×384, 32 samples and denoising (lines 164–210).

The available step-1 execution actually logged 16/16 samples despite its build specifying 32, and saved a PNG and blend with null error and empty stderr (X1259, `steps/001/build.py`, lines 169–174; X1260, `steps/001/result.json`, lines 2–7). The aggregate record reports three CPU executions, completion and no runtime error; no step-3 execution log is supplied here. It records overall .3635 and functional passes for `bank_00`, again with semantic completeness and support/collision truth null (X1256, `record.json`, lines 16–53, 58–86).

**Limit:** These are completed or reported-complete reconstructions, not evidence of visual fidelity. No reference or rendered images were provided for inspection. Coordinates, grouped parts and operability passes do not establish physical contact, correct assembly, or image quality; recorded scores and selections are not independent quality acceptance.
